stderr: م قد أخذت القرآن كله وما يدريه ما كله","mentions":[]},{"verses":["89:1"],"words":["*"],"type":"sciences","speaker":"author","stance":"rejects","claim":"Alusi rejects the polemical claim that the Qur’an’s present form proves it was already collected as one complete codex in the Prophet’s lifetime; the cited evidence does not establish that.","anchor":"ومن لم يجعل الله له نورا فماله من نور","mentions":["24:40"]},{"verses":["89:1"],"words":["*"],"type":"sciences","speaker":"author","stance":"holds","claim":"He accepts that the Qur’an’s verses and suras were ordered as now and recited from memory in the Prophet’s time while written on separate materials; he rejects the claim that it was then one bound codex.","anchor":"إن القرآن كان على عهد رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم مجموعا مؤلفا على ما هو عليه الآن","mentions":[]},{"verses":["89:1"],"words":["*"],"type":"sciences","speaker":"author","stance":"holds","claim":"Alusi says the standard codex has 114 suras by accepted consensus, with a reported count of 113 if al-Anfāl and Barāʾah are counted as one.","anchor":"في مصحفنا مائة وأربعة عشرة","mentions":[]},{"verses":["89:1"],"words":["*"],"type":"sciences","speaker":"author","stance":"rejects","claim":"Alusi says Ibn Masʿūd’s codex had 112 suras; he omitted the protective suras, reportedly called them prayers, and no Companion followed him. Since he recited them in prayer, Alusi rejects the claim that he only opposed writing them.","anchor":"وفي مصحف ابن مسعود مائة وإثنتا عشرة سورة لأنه لم يكتب المعوذتين بل صح عنه أنه كان يحكهما من المصاحف","mentions":[]},{"verses":["89:1"],"words":["*"],"type":"sciences","speaker":"author","stance":"reports","claim":"Alusi says Ubayy’s codex had 115 suras, including al-Khalaʿ and al-Ḥafd, and combined al-Fīl with Quraysh as one sura.","anchor":"وفي مصحف أبي خمسة عشرة لأنه كتب في آخره","mentions":[]},{"verses":["89:1"],"words":["الفجر"],"type":"sciences","speaker":"author","stance":"reports","claim":"Alusi lists divergent codex orders: Ibn Masʿūd placed al-Fajr after al-Taḥrīm; Ubayy placed al-Isrāʾ after al-Kahf, al-Ḥujurāt after Nūn, al-Mulk after al-Ḥujurāt, al-Nāziʿāt after al-Wāqiʿah, and al-Sharḥ after al-Ikhlāṣ.","anchor":"وسورة ( بني إسرائيل ) في مصحف أبي بعد ( الكهف )","mentions":[]},{"verses":["89:1"],"words":["*"],"type":"sciences","speaker":"author","stance":"holds","claim":"Alusi says attribution of the codex collection to ʿUthmān and his companions is widely established, even among Shiʿis, and attributes denials to sectarian prejudice.","anchor":"مع أن نسبة هذا الجمع إليهما من أوضح الأمور بل أشهر من المشهور وهو شائع أيضا عند الشيعة","mentions":[]},{"verses":["89:1"],"words":["*"],"type":"sciences","speaker":"author","stance":"holds","claim":"Alusi concludes that the order of both verses and suras is prophetic; he says verse order is unquestionably fixed and cites a consensus reported by al-Zarkashī and Abū Jaʿfar.","anchor":"فأعلم أن ترتيب آية وسوره بتوقيف من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم","mentions":[]}]}
